title: Content-Security-Policy worker-src allows plaintext HTTP sources
description: The Content-Security-Policy worker-src directive lists the scheme source `http:`, either alone or beside other sources, so the browser may load worker scripts over plaintext HTTP. A network attacker who can answer that request supplies the worker scripts himself, and the response that carries the policy is not the response that decides what loads.
remediation: Remove `http:` from worker-src and name the exact HTTPS origins that are needed. If a legacy origin still serves over HTTP, terminate TLS in front of it and list the HTTPS name instead of relaxing the directive.
limitation: One header value and one directive. The rule reports the scheme token in worker-src only; when worker-src is absent the default-src fallback decides, and other rules report that case. It cannot tell whether the plaintext origin is reachable from the browser that receives the policy.
